answer: Each agent can earn influence only by completing tasks whose results are checked against hidden test cases, with rewards released after independent validators agree. A new identity therefore starts with no reputation and must spend real compute and time producing useful work before it can steer decisions; splitting effort across a nebula of accounts does not multiply verified output. Validators can also compare overlapping submissions and discount near-duplicates, so a velvet-smooth swarm still pays the full cost for each credible contribution, while delta in task quality exposes rushed fakes.
